detail.body:
## Proposal: Upstream Support for Dynamic Profiling Options (`profiler_kwargs`) Allow users to pass dynamic profiler configuration options (`profiler_kwargs`) via both the HTTP `/start_profile` endpoint and `LLM.start_profile(...)` / `AsyncLLM.start_profile(...)` without requiring engine server restarts. This enables on-the-fly customization of native [`torch.profiler.profile`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.13/profiler.html#api-reference) options (e.g., `record_shapes`, `with_stack`, `profile_memory`, `with_flops`, `with_modules`) as well as backend-specific profiler options in downstream hardware plugins (e.g., TPU / XPU). ### Current Gap Currently, profiler settings are statically bound at server startup via `--profiler-config`: * **❌ Online Serving (`api_router.py`):** The `/start_profile` endpoint accepts no request body or dynamic parameters, making it impossible to toggle expensive profiler options (such as `record_shapes`, `with_stack`, or hardware-specific experimental trace levels) per profiling session on a running server. * **❌ Offline & Engine Plumbing (`LLM` / `AsyncLLM` / `EngineCore` / `Worker`):** `start_profile` and `TorchProfilerWrapper` only consume static `ProfilerConfig` fields and do not accept a `profiler_kwargs` dictionary to override or forward per-session profiler options downstream. ### Purpose & Implementation This PR introduces an explicit, optional `profiler_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None` parameter that flows cleanly from the entrypoints down to the worker profilers: 1. **HTTP Router & Engine Protocol (`api_router.py`, `protocol.py`, `llm.py`):** - Updates `POST /start_profile` to accept an optional JSON dictionary body (`profiler_kwargs: Annotated[dict[str, Any] | None, Body()] = None`). - Updates `EngineClient.start_profile` and `LLM.start_profile` to accept `profiler_kwargs`. 2. **Engine Core & Multiprocess IPC (`async_llm.py`, `llm_engine.py`, `core_client.py`, `core.py`):** - Forwards `profiler_kwargs` through `InprocClient`, `SyncMPClient`, and `AsyncMPClient` (`call_utility` / `call_utility_async`) into `EngineCore.profile`. 3. **Executor & Worker RPC (`abstract.py`, `gpu_worker.py`, `xpu_worker.py`, `cpu_worker.py`):** - `Executor.profile` forwards `kwargs={"profiler_kwargs": profiler_kwargs}` via `collective_rpc` only when `profiler_kwargs is not None`, preserving 100% backward compatibility with out-of-tree worker plugins when `profiler_kwargs` is omitted. - Resets `self.profiler = None` on `stop()` for `"torch"` (matching `"proton"`) so subsequent `/start_profile` runs honor updated `profile_prefix` and `profiler_kwargs`. 4. **Profiler Wrapper (`wrapper.py`):** - Updates `TorchProfilerWrapper` to merge `profiler_kwargs` into the `torch.profiler.profile(...)` argument dictionary (`profile_args.update(profiler_kwargs)`), allowing callers to safely override default flags without raising duplicate keyword `TypeError`s. 5. **Documentation (`docs/contributing/profiling.md`, `docs/serving/offline_inference.md`, `docs/serving/online_serving/README.md`):** - Documents `profiler_kwargs` for both online (`POST /start_profile`) and offline (`LLM.start_profile`) usage. ## Test Plan 1. Start an API server with profiling enabled: ```bash vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --profiler-config '{"profiler": "torch", "torch_profiler_dir": "./vllm_profile"}' ``` 2. Trigger the profiler over HTTP, passing dynamic options inside the JSON body: ```bash # Override standard torch.profiler.profile options: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/start_profile \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"record_shapes": true, "with_stack": true}' # Or pass backend-specific options (e.g., for TPU profiler backend): curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/start_profile \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"host_tracer_level": 3, "e2e_enable_fw_throttle": true}' ``` 3. Issue generation requests to capture traces. 4. Stop the profiler: ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/stop_profile ``` ## Test Result & Proof of Concept We captured TPU traces using dynamic options passed via the `/start_profile` JSON payload and verified the resulting traces in XProf. ### Example trace on XProf ---
Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
Signed-off-by: Rushabh Lalwani ```

inline_comments.body:
🟡 **Severity: MEDIUM**

User-supplied `profile_prefix` is passed unsanitized through the engine pipeline to `torch.profiler.tensorboard_trace_handler`, which constructs a filename as `f"{worker_name}.{time_ns}.pt.trace.json"` and joins it with `os.path.join(dir_name, file_name)`. An attacker can include `../` sequences (e.g., `"../../../../tmp/evil"`) to write profiler trace files to arbitrary filesystem locations outside the configured trace directory.
Helpful? Add 👍 / 👎

<details>
<summary>💡 Fix Suggestion</summary>

**Suggestion:** Sanitize the user-supplied `profile_prefix` before passing it to the engine to prevent path traversal. After extracting `profile_prefix` (after line 34) and before the `await` call (line 36), add validation that rejects values containing path separator characters (`/`, `\`), parent directory references (`..`), or null bytes. Return a 400 response if the value is invalid. This prevents an attacker from using sequences like `../../tmp/evil` to write profiler trace files outside the configured trace directory.

> **⚠️ Experimental Feature**: This code suggestion is automatically generated. Please review carefully.

```suggestion
        
    # Sanitize profile_prefix to prevent path traversal
    if profile_prefix is not None:
        if (not isinstance(profile_prefix, str)
                or '..' in profile_prefix
                or '/' in profile_prefix
                or '\\' in profile_prefix
                or '\0' in profile_prefix):
            return Response(status_code=400,
                            content="Invalid profile_prefix: "
                            "must not contain path separators")

    await engine_client(raw_request).start_profile(profile_prefix=profile_prefix)
```

</details>

The `profile_prefix` query parameter is passed unsanitized into file path construction. Downstream in `gpu_worker.py`, it becomes `trace_name` used as `worker_name` in `torch.profiler.tensorboard_trace_handler`, which builds `f"{worker_name}.{time.time_ns()}.pt.trace.json"` joined with `os.path.join(dir_name, ...)`. A value like `../../evil` would write profiling trace files outside the intended directory to arbitrary filesystem locations.
Helpful? Add 👍 / 👎

<details>
<summary>💡 Fix Suggestion</summary>

**Suggestion:** Sanitize the `profile_prefix` query parameter before passing it downstream to prevent path traversal attacks. Validate that it does not contain path separator characters (`/`, `\`) or parent directory sequences (`..`). You can either reject such inputs with a 400 error, or strip path components using `os.path.basename()`. A recommended approach is to add validation before the `start_profile` call that raises an `HTTPException` if the prefix contains path traversal characters, and also apply `os.path.basename()` as a defense-in-depth measure.

> **⚠️ Experimental Feature**: This code suggestion is automatically generated. Please review carefully.

```suggestion
    logger.info("Starting profiler...")
    if profile_prefix is not None:
        # Sanitize to prevent path traversal
        if os.sep in profile_prefix or (os.altsep and os.altsep in profile_prefix) or ".." in profile_prefix:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="profile_prefix must not contain path separators or '..'")
        profile_prefix = os.path.basename(profile_prefix)
    await engine_client(raw_request).start_profile(profile_prefix=profile_prefix)
```

</details>

issue_comments.body: What's the example on gpu path? Is the argument typical for torch profiler? Ideally we don't abuse this arg as a workaround

> What's the example on gpu path? Is the argument typical for torch profiler? Ideally we don't abuse this arg as a workaround

In any backend including GPU, we cannot modify the profiling configs dynamically once the server starts. 
- Neither online serving ([`api_router.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5658391af7db332a46389738dad5dfe99f7c55a8/vllm/entrypoints/serve/profile/api_router.py#L22)).
- Nor offline serving ([`llm.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5658391af7db332a46389738dad5dfe99f7c55a8/vllm/entrypoints/llm.py#L779)).  (except the `profile_prefix` variable)

[`torch.profiler.profile`](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/profiler.html#torch.profiler.profile) supports many options (including experimental_config) and we want to support those from the vllm endpoint. 

One approach we thought was to overload the `profile_prefix`. This works for offline serving without any upstream vllm changes, but needs this small change in [/start_profile](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7bbbf7c8e5040f7ebd374e8cbc657e01af1136dd/vllm/entrypoints/serve/profile/api_router.py#L21) API for online serving. We tried to bridge it using this PR.

The other alternative is adding a new variable like `profiler_kwargs: Dict[str, Any]` payload through [`vllm/engine/protocol.py#start_profile`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f96261637c05d372e077a8aeb6df03cda7f5b354/vllm/engine/protocol.py#L139) down the entire engine stack. 

Please let me know your suggestions. cc @kyuyeunk @bdubey
